content:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: v3.4.1 -> green (canary 10%) in us-east-1 at 1767501234

nina: got a page, spike of 502/503s from model gateway in eu-west-1, started ~1767501300. Seeing increased latencies for embed requests. :rotating_light:

samir: I'm looking at the rollout dashboard — only 10% to green, but DNS weighted update pushed 20% to green for eu-west-1 by mistake. Investigating policy mismatch between regions.

jordan: pinging infra — can we confirm if blue/green DNS weight config was applied wrong? also, which customers hit eu-west?

elaine: Support: large customers ACorp and BetaApps reported errors. ACorp has ~15% of requests in eu-west. They're seeing consistent 503s. 

miguel: checking loadbalancer health — some green nodes in eu-west failed healthcheck and were marked draining, but DNS weight was still routing to them (TTL 60s). Looks like healthcheck probe path changed in v3.4.1.

nina: on-call note: paging PD-4321 -> severity P1. Current mitigation: try kill-switch for green, then rollback if kill-switch doesn't cut traffic due to DNS TTL.

samir: quick command to flip feature flag kill-switch for rollout: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" \"https://flag.internal/api/toggle?flag=rolling-green&value=off\"`

miguel: executed kill-switch at 1767501380. API returned 200. DNS still routing ~12% to green (clients caching old DNS).

deploy-bot: Canary health check failures detected in eu-west-1: 6/10 green instances unhealthy. Auto-fallback did not trigger because weight config override present.

jordan: since DNS TTL = 60s, some edge caches will hold onto new answers up to 1m. We need immediate rollback on the service side to prevent 503s if kill-switch ineffective. Samir, can we rollback to v3.4.0 in eu-west-1-only?

samir: starting region-scoped rollback: `redwood rollout rollback --version=3.4.0 --region=eu-west-1 --force` (will preserve blue box config). Executed at 1767501455.

miguel: I also cleared LB cache and re-synced health checks for green nodes. Pushed a probe-fix to the healthcheck path as a hotfix: `/healthz` -> `/status/ready` mapping.

elaine: customer impact update: error rate for ACorp dropped from 22% to 6% after rollback started. BetaApps still seeing intermittent errors from EU mobile users. Logging shows stale DNS resolved to green VIPs that are draining.

nina: contacting BetaApps CSM to advise retry/backoff guidance and that we're rolling back. Sending incident update.

deploy-bot: Rollback to 3.4.0 in eu-west-1 completed at 1767501540. Traffic to green should be 0% in region after DNS propagation and LB sync.

samir: note: the root cause is a canary packaging change that accidentally changed the probe endpoint and a deployment pipeline step incorrectly incremented DNS weight for eu-west. I'll open a postmortem.

jordan: thanks. For live mitigation checklist: (1) Kill-switch toggled at 1767501380, (2) region rollback executed at 1767501455, (3) LB cache cleared at 1767501495, (4) rollback confirmed 1767501540.

miguel: confirm: EU error rate back to baseline ~0.5% at 1767501620. Some edge clients still show 503s until TTL expires — expected ~60s window.

elaine: Customer outreach: ACorp acknowledged, BetaApps on a support call now. No data loss reported. Agent noted request retries succeeded after 30s.

nina: handing off to jordan for postmortem and follow-up (on-call shift ends). Jordan is primary SRE lead.

jordan: taking handoff. I'll file incident PD-4321, include timeline, commands executed, and action items: fix probe path in pipeline, add a gating check that ensures DNS weight changes must be globally consistent across regions, and add automated rollback on >=5% error within 5 minutes for region canaries.

samir: creating PR to revert the probe change and to add a pipeline assert for DNS weight (PR #2987).

deploy-bot: Incident summary posted to /incidents/PD-4321 at 1767501800. Severity P1, resolved for now.

jordan: final note for runbook updates: add step to verify LB probe endpoints before allowing DNS weight changes; reduce canary DNS weight TTL or add service-level immediate routing override capability.

nina: thanks team — I'll update the on-call log and close the page once postmortem link exists. :thumbsup:
